purpose: Acceptance of documentation work only. Not proof of implementation correctness.
rules: Retain existing implementation IDs and valid evidence.
This document checklist is a separate task scope, not a replacement implementation ledger.
A row needs actual document evidence and independent review before verification.
Future code and automated enforcement remain pending.

items.requirement: Record the actual branch tips and task start commit.
items.acceptance: Record exact refs without changing or resetting the repository.

items.requirement: Reconcile the baseline branch with the frozen tag.
items.acceptance: Compare source, manifests, fixtures, and capture inputs. State the limits of each comparison.

items.requirement: Inspect all five reported commits and their parents.
items.acceptance: Read omitted patches through parent/child blobs. Record a finding or a justified disposition for each commit.

items.requirement: Trace each reported mechanism to current consumers.
items.acceptance: Separate a historical change from a currently reachable defect.

items.requirement: Find related patterns in all four preview apps.
items.acceptance: Audit raw painting, generated frames, fixture-specific dispatch, and normal input/layer bypasses.

items.requirement: Read existing instructions and canonical planning documents.
items.acceptance: Map root and scoped instructions, component contracts, task records, and checklist views.

items.requirement: Define the preview-app purpose.
items.acceptance: Describe Showcase, Jackin Preview, Holla, and TablePro as complete UI previews built from reusable components.

items.requirement: Define the conjunction of acceptance requirements.
items.acceptance: Require pixels, interactions, ownership, public APIs, customization, and review together.

items.requirement: Define the low-level author boundary.
items.acceptance: Permit rendering inside approved reusable components. Prohibit its use as a preview escape hatch.

items.requirement: Define the data-versus-screen distinction.
items.acceptance: Permit fixture records and child terminal content. Prohibit exported full-screen answer data.

items.requirement: Define normal and paused execution rules.
items.acceptance: The motion policy cannot bypass component input, layer opening, or routing.

items.requirement: Define the missing-component procedure.
items.acceptance: Require a smallest reusable primitive contract and an implementation owner. Do not fix code now.

items.requirement: Define legitimate responsive layout.
items.acceptance: Separate constrained layout and semantic breakpoints from snapshot-size-specific painters.

items.requirement: Preserve the current multi-crate responsibility model.
items.acceptance: Resolve stale one-crate text. Do not count crates as evidence of reusable behavior.

items.requirement: Map all 45 existing component contracts.
items.acceptance: Every required surface retains one canonical owner and its detailed behaviors.

items.requirement: Map all shared foundations and legacy dispositions.
items.acceptance: Keep all declared shared mechanisms and historical-family obligations accounted for.

items.requirement: Use one component document template.
items.acceptance: Specify data, state, phases, responses, variants, parts, bounds, and verification requirements.

items.requirement: Separate current and proposed API signatures.
items.acceptance: Do not present the earlier proposed TextInput signature as current source.

items.requirement: Write complete control and field usage examples.
items.acceptance: Show phase separation, controlled state, typed responses, disabled and invalid cases.

items.requirement: Write collection and layout examples.
items.acceptance: Show keyed data, content descriptions, responsive regions, and state reconciliation.

items.requirement: Write overlay, picker, and menu examples.
items.acceptance: Show normal layer opening, cancellation, nesting, and target identity.

items.requirement: Write data, output, and motion examples.
items.acceptance: Show Grid capabilities, logs, code/diff, motion sampling, and prepared terminal content.

items.requirement: Write all four preview composition examples.
items.acceptance: Document each helper as component composition or a data reducer. No hidden painter is permitted.

items.requirement: Write supported customization examples.
items.acceptance: Show variants and semantic patches. Separate advanced authoring from normal consumption.

items.requirement: Write negative examples from the findings.
items.acceptance: Include historical frame dispatch, repainted controls, and disguised snapshot components.

items.requirement: Record every example status and unresolved helper.
items.acceptance: Use the example catalog. Include source or compile evidence only when actually obtained.

items.requirement: Require independent plan review for each work item.
items.acceptance: Review scope, owner, needed component contracts, and evidence before implementation work.

items.requirement: Require independent review before every commit.
items.acceptance: Apply this rule to documentation, tests, generated code, metadata, and implementation.

items.requirement: Bind review to an exact subject.
items.acceptance: Record parent commit, candidate tree, binary diff digest, and all changed paths.

items.requirement: Invalidate approval after any subject change.
items.acceptance: Do not reuse an earlier approval after edits or a changed base.

items.requirement: Bind approved subjects to actual commits.
items.acceptance: Verify committed parent/tree and store the actual SHA in an external receipt.

items.requirement: Require final work-item integration review.
items.acceptance: Per-commit reviews do not replace the complete work-item check.

items.requirement: Preserve frequent coherent commits.
items.acceptance: Request review promptly. Frequency does not permit review bypass.

items.requirement: Separate file integrity from live parity.
items.acceptance: State what a store-integrity run does and does not establish.

items.requirement: Specify component-ownership proof.
items.acceptance: Trace calls and run targeted painter/action mutations in future implementation work.

items.requirement: Specify fixture-independent behavior checks.
items.acceptance: Change labels, order, dimensions, origins, and input paths to expose stored answers.

items.requirement: Specify six-format capture and trust boundaries.
items.acceptance: Retain ANSI, HTML, PNG, ASCII, TXT, JSON, companions, manifest lineage, and separate admission.

items.requirement: Specify exact current-default parity.
items.acceptance: Use independent reference/candidate captures, structural cells, cursor/state, and exact pixels under qualified profiles.

items.requirement: Specify real interaction and state coverage.
items.acceptance: Require events, transitions, targets, actions, and timing, not only assigned visual flags.

items.requirement: Specify exact required-case/checkpoint aggregation.
items.acceptance: Missing, stale, failed, cancelled, or required-skipped evidence must not count as success.

items.requirement: Specify enforcement status honestly.
items.acceptance: Mark checks as existing/source-checked, executed, or specified for later work. Do not claim hooks or CI were installed.

items.requirement: Preserve existing checklist IDs and valid evidence.
items.acceptance: Reopen only unsupported or stale statuses with a recorded reason and prior receipt.

items.requirement: Separate document acceptance from code-remediation tasks.
items.acceptance: Known code defects remain pending. Their presence does not mean these document edits have fixed them.

items.requirement: Update AGENTS, GOAL, summaries, and scoped instructions.
items.acceptance: Make rules reachable at task start. Preserve sign-off and CLAUDE symlink conventions.

items.requirement: Reconcile duplicate architecture and API authorities.
items.acceptance: Use links to canonical contracts. Remove contradictory current instructions.

items.requirement: Update task and PR review templates.
items.acceptance: Require component ownership and exact-subject evidence. Do not alter executable verifier logic.

items.requirement: Use controlled English and a project glossary.
items.acceptance: Use active short instructions and consistent technical terms. Record language-check limitations.

items.requirement: Check document links, JSON, IDs, and example labels.
items.acceptance: Run deterministic document-pack validation without treating it as runtime validation.

items.requirement: Prove the task changed only allowed documents.
items.acceptance: Compare with the task start. Source, tests, build inputs, workflows, and approvals remain unchanged.

items.requirement: Obtain a fresh final documentation review.
items.acceptance: The reviewer did not author the integrated documents. Resolve confirmed findings.

items.requirement: Publish a factual final documentation report.
items.acceptance: List reviewed commits, document checks, example status, and pending code/enforcement work.
